invocation: claude-code-cli interactive session (Claude Code; actual runtime model claude-sonnet-5-5); read-only audit of 73563404e..9132beaa0 with deterministic re-runs

findings.title: Unguarded mcp>=1.0.0 remains at non-allowlisted entrypoints
findings.body: services/mcp-client/services/mcp-client/requirements.txt, leantime-bridge/requirements.txt and mcp-client-python/setup.py still declare mcp>=1.0.0 with no <2 bound. They are outside the write surface so leaving them is containment-correct. The leantime-bridge Dockerfile does not reference its requirements file. Follow-up: pin or confirm dead.

findings.title: No tests for dope-context behavior changes
findings.body: Packet S1 requires focused tests that reproduce old defects or assert repaired behavior. Only the CLI lazy-import test was added. Nothing covers the pypdf-then-PyPDF2 import order, the guarded tiktoken.get_encoding degrade path, or the narrowed except in get_chunk_complexity. The Qdrant contract test in the receipts predates this change (base commit 5048571db).

findings.title: Uncommitted uv.lock modification in worktree (+27 lines)
findings.body: Adds pypdf, python-magic and tiktoken after the pyproject edit, apparently from a non-frozen uv run. The candidate commit is clean and the DEP integrator owns uv.lock. It must not be staged or pushed with this packet; revert with git checkout -- uv.lock after audit closure. Committed pyproject.toml and uv.lock are inconsistent until the DEP integrator regenerates the lock. The dope-context image build is unaffected because its Dockerfile copies only pyproject.toml.

findings.title: Third lazy-import test requires litellm installed and is a weak regression guard
findings.body: test_sync_litellm_database_imports_litellm_lazily asserts litellm in sys.modules, so it fails in an environment without litellm, where the new ImportError branch is taken. That branch has no direct test. The test runs in-process and passes against base when dopemux resolves to the candidate source. The two subprocess tests are the real guards and both fail on base as verified.

findings.title: tiktoken pre-warm makes the dope-context image build require egress
findings.body: The build downloads the cl100k_base BPE file from openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net and fails hard if it is unreachable. This is fail-closed by design. No image was built, so the pre-warm is untested.

findings.title: Packet S1 items not evidenced in the diff
findings.body: Qdrant SDK import contract fix was already present at base (5048571db). Docker/vendor context pollution guard: no .dockerignore was touched and it is not on the allowlist. The dope-context image build context is the repo root, so the root .dockerignore governs (the service-level one is not applied). It excludes .git, __pycache__, caches, .venv, node_modules and *.log, but has no logs/ or data/ directory pattern. Neither services/dope-context/logs nor data exists in this worktree, so no pollution was observed. Whether the S1 item required a change is for the supervisor to decide.

findings.title: Requested return shape conflicts with embedded_audit.schema.json
findings.body: The task requested verdict/runner/model/runtime_family/checked_head/base_sha. The schema sets additionalProperties false, requires different keys and has no claude-sonnet-5-5 enum value. This file follows the schema (auditor_model sonnet; literal model id in invocation). Identity fields are in sidecar AUDIT_RETURN.identity.json.
